solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: European fellow entertaining star, having party somewhere in UK

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside your home, so the first word holds what follows

blocks.note: a star performer is an ace

explanation.surface: A man from the Continent hosts a celebrity and throws a party somewhere in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The fellow is the outer shell: everything after him goes inside. NI is Northern Ireland, part of the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Macedonia, the Balkan country, is a European by birth.

clue.text: Fluid and second fluid in the body

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
bile is a digestive fluid made by the liver

explanation.surface: Liquids within the human body.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Fluid' is an adjective meaning free-moving, not a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile and fluid both describe something able to move or change freely, as adjectives.

clue.text: Peasant and tot sitting awkwardly in vehicle

indicators.note: a child sitting awkwardly is twisted round, so the word's letters are disordered
in places the jumbled word inside the vehicle, as a passenger rides within

explanation.surface: A farmhand and a toddler squashed uncomfortably into a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottar was a Scottish farm labourer living in a cottage, a type of peasant.

clue.text: Nice guide led off with precautionary steps to avoid trouble

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong, as food goes off, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A pleasant tour leader set off, taking care to avoid problems.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice looks like the French city or an adjective; it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Due diligence is the careful investigation done before a deal so as not to be caught out.

clue.text: It’s clear son is hiding in den

indicators.note: hiding in a place means being concealed inside it, so the letter sits within the other word

blocks.note: net, or nett, means clear after deductions

explanation.surface: Obviously the boy is lurking in his room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is part of the fragment for NET: profit that is clear of costs.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest and a den are both snug retreats or animal lairs, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Notice star leading fashion, upright character being held in high regard

indicators.note: being held means being clasped inside, so the single letter goes within the word before

blocks.note: Mira is a variable star in Cetus
ton is an old word for fashion, as in bon ton
the capital letter I is a single upright stroke

explanation.surface: Spot a celebrity leading the fashion world, a person of upright character who is widely esteemed.
explanation.walkthrough: Mira is a named star, not a celebrity; ton is an old word for the fashionable world; the upright character is the capital letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiration is respect and warm approval, which is holding someone in high regard.

clue.text: Group having drink before start of meal

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

explanation.surface: A party of people have a cuppa before they sit down to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a set of people working or playing together, a kind of group.

clue.text: Lovers should express them — so no time to be wasted!

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined, so the letters lose their order

explanation.surface: Romantic advice: declare your love now, there is no time to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers are urged to show their feelings, and feelings are what this word names.

clue.text: Pulpy stuff brought to kitchen? You may eat it

blocks.note: a kitchen is an example of a room, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Something soft carried into the kitchen to be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A mushroom is an edible fungus, so a cook or diner might eat one.

clue.text: Irritating bishop gets round the church HQ, having grabbed head of staff

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so just that is taken
grabbing something means holding it, so the church base wraps round the letter

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Rome is the headquarters of the Catholic Church

explanation.surface: A tiresome bishop visits the Vatican and grabs one of the staff on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside ROME, just after the R, giving RSOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bothersome causes annoyance, so it is irritating, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Trips to buy things beginning to end

indicators.note: the word's beginning letter is moved to its end, rotating it one place

blocks.note: to shop is to buy things

explanation.surface: Shopping excursions.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the S of SHOP from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Hops are short journeys, as in a quick flight, so they are brief trips.

clue.text: Redeveloped city alarms me, lacking a logical design?

indicators.note: a redeveloped area is rebuilt in a new layout, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone appalled by an urban regeneration scheme without sensible planning.
explanation.definitionFit: Asymmetrical means without balanced proportions, which a solver may read as lacking orderly planned design.

clue.text: Preamble has spacing between printed lines reduced slightly

indicators.note: cut down by only a little, so just the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: leading (pronounced 'ledding') is the printer's term for space between lines, once made with strips of lead

explanation.surface: An introduction where the typesetting has been tightened a touch.
explanation.walkthrough: LEADING loses its last letter G to give LEAD-IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead-in is introductory material before the main matter, which is what a preamble is.

clue.text: Cheaper wood has one making attempt to get hold of it

indicators.note: getting hold of something means grasping it, so one word clasps the other

blocks.note: a trier is someone who tries

explanation.surface: Someone trying to grab some lower-grade timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' points back to the wood, so the tree goes inside the person making an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashier means more like trash, so of lower quality: cheaper in the sense of shoddier.

clue.text: Huge number, male or female, given work at home, love to get stuck in

indicators.note: getting stuck in means being lodged inside, so the round letter sits within

blocks.note: male and female are the two sexes
to till is to work the soil
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A vast crowd of men and women, all working from home, falling in love.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextillion is ten to the power twenty-one, an enormous figure.

clue.text: Musical piece Verdi arranged with tempo not unusual

indicators.note: arranging music suggests putting notes into a new order, so the composer's name is reordered
something unusual is out of its normal form, so the small word is jumbled

explanation.surface: A Verdi score rearranged at a tempo that is perfectly normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not unusual' reads like 'ordinary'; actually it means jumble NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A divertimento is a light instrumental composition, often for small ensemble, so a musical piece.

clue.text: Mineral I removed from ground glittered, not half

indicators.note: removing a letter from a word takes it away, leaving the rest
not half means only half survives, so the latter part is cut

blocks.note: a sports ground is a field

explanation.surface: A sparkling stone dug from the earth, after one fragment is taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: FIELD loses I; SPARKLED keeps its first half.
explanation.definitionFit: Feldspar is a common rock-forming silicate mineral found in granite.

clue.text: Complained with good drink allowed to seep away

blocks.note: a liquid that has bled has leaked or seeped out

explanation.surface: Someone moaned that their fine liquor had been left to leak out.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble is to mutter discontentedly, so grumbled means made a complaint.

clue.text: See one man try to change what is needed to secure contract?

definitions.text: what is needed to secure contract?

indicators.note: the letters are made to change their positions, giving a new order

explanation.surface: Watch a man attempt to alter the terms needed to clinch a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest money is a deposit paid as a pledge of good faith to bind a bargain or contract.

clue.text: Somewhere in India needing support — it’s hairy

definitions.note: a phrase describing a noun: the thing that is hairy

blocks.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A place in India that needs propping up, and things there are getting dicey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' also means risky, which suits the surface; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatee is a small pointed beard on the chin, a tuft of facial hair.

clue.text: Devon town not getting on — praise looked for

indicators.note: not getting something means doing without it, so those letters drop out

blocks.note: Crediton is a market town in Devon, a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: A Devon town that is not progressing yearns for recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not getting on' sounds like a stalled town; it says remove ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit is acknowledgement or recognition that people hope to receive for their work.

clue.text: Two notes one left in church where one lives?

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the church abbreviation

blocks.note: do and mi are notes of the sol-fa scale
CE is the Church of England
I is the Roman numeral one and L abbreviates left

explanation.surface: A churchgoer's home, with music sung in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A domicile is a legal or formal word for a person's home, the place they reside.

clue.text: Member needs your and my protection

blocks.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
what belongs to you and me is ours

explanation.surface: A club member wants you and me to look after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Armour is the protective metal covering worn in battle, a form of protection.

clue.text: Idiot in dress — the fellow getting thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out means ejected, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A fool in a frock as the man is ejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Clot is British informal for a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Ancient language in China and India

blocks.note: in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, so china is a pal
I is India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An old tongue spoken across China and India.
explanation.walkthrough: China looks like the country but is rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Pali is the classical Indian language of the Theravada Buddhist scriptures, so an ancient language.

clue.text: See inside record a fifties youngster regarded as ‘disturbed‘

indicators.note: inside places the first word within the second

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look or see
a Teddy boy, or Ted, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress

explanation.surface: A 1950s rebel listening to a record is thought to be troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the old exclamation, not a verb of vision; Teddy boys were the British youth cult of the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Dislocated can mean put out of place or thrown into confusion, close to disturbed.

clue.text: Journey made by newly-wed heading off?

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and off means it goes

explanation.surface: A honeymoon trip for a newly married person setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIDE loses its first letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride is a trip in a vehicle or on a horse, so a short journey.

clue.text: Line is written by this writer in second episode

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters within the word for a short moment

explanation.surface: An author writes a line in an episode of a serial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter's way of saying ME; the pair sits inside the word for a second.
explanation.definitionFit: An instalment is one part of a serial published or broadcast at intervals, so an episode.
